canonical_statement: The fundamental spatial geometry of the universe, as described by Newtonian gravity, is Euclidean.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: Consistently with Newtonian gravity, the background geometry is assumed to be Euclidean.

canonical_statement: There are infinitely many locally distinct but globally equivalent formulations of energy density in Newtonian gravitation.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: there is an infinite number of energy densities εa (x, t) (a continuous 1-parameter family described by a), which are locally different, but globally equivalent

canonical_statement: Locally distinct energy density formulations yield the same total gravitational energy when integrated over all space under specific boundary conditions.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: their distributions are different point-by-point in space, but when integrated over all space under suitable boundary conditions at spatial infinity... they return the same total gravitational energy Eg

canonical_statement: The fundamental balance of physical quantities is independent of the observer's reference frame.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: the balance itself is observer independent: it is a spacetime divergence of a four-quantity.

canonical_statement: The local balance of physical quantities is a representation of a covariant law within an external laboratory frame.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: The local balance is a laboratory frame version of the covariant law.

canonical_statement: The substantial balance of physical quantities represents the same covariant law as the local balance, but is expressed in a comoving frame using relative quantities from the laboratory frame.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: the substantial balance is the same in a comoving frame, but expressed with the relative quantities of the labframe.

canonical_statement: The bulk force of a gravitational field within a spatial region can be expressed as a surface traction on its boundary.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: the bulk force due to fg = ρg of the gravitational field g = −∇φ in any spatial region can be expressed as a surface traction on the boundary

canonical_statement: The classical holographic property of the gravitational field arises as a consequence of zero dissipation in ideal, dissipation-free continuous fields.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: the classical holographic property emerges as a consequence of zero dissipation

canonical_statement: The thermodynamic information necessary to define bulk equations of motion is entirely encoded by boundary fluxes.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: the thermodynamic information required to specify the bulk equations of motion...is entirely encoded by the boundary fluxes

canonical_statement: A classical system can be thermodynamically holographic while remaining kinematically volumetric.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: the classical weakly nonlocal fluid is thermodynamically holographic, yet kinematically volumetric

canonical_statement: The gravitational Lagrangian density describes the interaction between matter and gravity, and the intrinsic nature of the gravitational field.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: the pure gravitational term...describes the gravitational field 'on its own', while the coupling term...describes the 'inter-action' of matter ρ and gravity φ.

canonical_statement: In the context of the gravitational Lagrangian, mass density is considered a fixed, a priori parametric variable, not a dynamically variable field.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: mass density distribution ρ(x, t)=fixed, given a priori, regarded as a 'parametric variable (function)', but not as a dynamically variable field itself.

canonical_statement: Matter dictates the distribution of gravity in space, but gravity does not reciprocally influence the motion of matter.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: matter tells gravity how to spread in space, but gravity does not (yet) tell matter how to move

canonical_statement: The gravitational field is derived from a more fundamental scalar field.

attributions.chapter: ON THE ENERGY BALANCE OF NEWTONIAN GRAVITATION
attributions.surface_quote: g = −∇φ as an ”auxiliary” vector field, derived from the more fundamental scalar field φ
